data.name: Tap Tap Infinity
data.detailed_description:
Monsters are attacking! Click to defeat them, save the village! Love Clicker/Incremental games? Inspired by Clicker Heroes, Tap Tap Infinity takes things to the next level with tactical Hero and Spell upgrades, an XP/Rank system, an unfolding story, fancy-pants 3d monsters and environments, endless gameplay, cross-platform cloud syncing and awesome graphics. Super-simple to play ... but with more strategic depth if you want it!



Level up your Heroes so that they farm gold and search for the fabled Infinity Tokens, even while you're not playing! Earn XP by defeating monsters and clearing levels to unlock mighty Spells and gain a DPS bonus per Rank! Get to a high enough Rank and Ascend over and over to gain double the DPS bonus per Rank each Ascension.



Find the Tokens of Infinity and trade them to the Guardians to unlock Powers. With 16 different Powers to choose from you can customize the game to play how *you* want it. 'Go Infinite' to restart at level 1 but with your Infinity Tokens multiplying your DPS so you can reach further and further into the game as you try to ultimately defeat 'The Master' !



Tap Tap Infinity is free to play and incredibly easy to get into:

★ Click monsters to kill them and collect their gold.
★ Hire the beaten Boss monsters to help you do extra damage as you level them up.
★ Your Heroes earn gold for you while you're not playing, even if the game is closed.
★ Find Valor Points and use them to Upgrade your Heroes, doubling how powerful their Skills are!
★ Gain XP and unlock Spells to auto-click, do more damage or even skip instantly between Boss levels!
★ Find Infinity Tokens to start all over again but with a permanent boost to your DPS.
★ Trade Infinity Tokens to The Guardians of Infinity for Powers that customize the game play or use them to upgrade Spells to make them more powerful.
★ Save your game to the cloud and keep playing on mobile!

The game is already live on iTunes (4.5/5 star rating) and Google Play (4.4/5 star rating). Looking to discuss the game or check in with the TTI community? Check out the subreddit:

Tap Tap Infinity was built by Scary Bee LLC, a one-man coffee-fueled indie game studio in Seattle.

data.short_description: Tap Tap Infinity is a fully 3D incremental RPG. Hire Heroes to fight for you, even with the game closed! Gain unimaginable DPS, mountains of gold, conquer thousands of levels and millions of monsters on your quest to defeat ‘The Master'.

reviews.review:
Tap Tap Infinity is an incremental clicker game built around the simple idea of defeating monsters, earning gold and using that gold to make my team stronger. The basic loop is straightforward: I tap to help attack enemies, earn rewards and purchase upgrades that allow me to progress through increasingly difficult stages.

The biggest strength for me is the satisfying progression. Every few minutes I can usually afford another upgrade, unlock a stronger hero or improve my damage output. Watching the numbers grow gives the game a surprisingly addictive quality, even though the actual interaction is very simple.

The hero system adds some variety to the otherwise basic clicking formula. Different heroes contribute different abilities and bonuses, so deciding where to spend my resources gives me more to think about than simply tapping as quickly as possible. Building a stronger team makes later stages feel like a reward for the time I have invested.

The idle mechanics are also convenient. Once my heroes become strong enough, they can continue making progress without requiring constant attention. I can leave the game running, return later and collect the rewards I have accumulated. That makes it easy to fit into short sessions or play alongside other activities.

The game is accessible as well. I do not need to understand complicated strategies before I can start making progress. The basic mechanics are immediately clear, and the various upgrades gradually introduce additional systems as I continue playing.

The biggest weakness is the repetitive nature of the core loop. Most of the time I am still defeating monsters, collecting gold and buying upgrades. Once the initial excitement of seeing numbers increase wears off, there may not be enough meaningful interaction to keep me engaged.

The progression can also become increasingly dependent on waiting and grinding. Eventually, upgrades become more expensive and enemies become stronger, which can make advancement feel slower. That is a normal part of incremental games, but it can make the later stages feel less satisfying than the early ones.

The presentation is colourful and functional, with the fantasy setting giving the game a little more personality than a completely abstract clicker. The characters and monsters help make the progression feel more tangible, even though the underlying gameplay remains very simple.

Overall, Tap Tap Infinity is a solid incremental game that understands the appeal of constant progression. I like the growing numbers, hero upgrades and convenient idle mechanics, while the repetitive gameplay and increasingly slow progression limit its long-term appeal. It works best when I want a simple game that can provide small rewards without demanding my full attention.

Rating: 7/10
